## Purpose

Use this separate workflow to create an approved CVD mortality metric release
from the authorised death-certificate source. It does not reuse the CVD event
preparation pathway.

## Before starting

- Confirm the release year and month and the operator's authority.
- Work on the authorised workstation with the private workspace available.
- Confirm the configured mortality REDCap credential is available to Step 1.
- Confirm **User > BNR > Update CVD mortality dashboard** is present in Stata.

## Six steps

1. **Extract mortality data.** Run Step 1 and check the month-end and record count. [Technical detail](../../technical/workflows/mortality/extract.qmd)
2. **Classify CVD deaths.** Run Step 2 and review the private classification outputs. The BNR approximate classifier is not formal national underlying-cause coding. [Technical detail](../../technical/workflows/mortality/classify.qmd)
3. **Build mortality burden data.** Run Step 3 and verify the count, proportion and rate outputs, reporting scope and QA. [Technical detail](../../technical/workflows/mortality/build-burden.qmd)
4. **Review the release.** Run Step 4 and complete analytical, classification and disclosure review of the candidate. [Technical detail](../../technical/workflows/mortality/review.qmd)
5. **Approve the reviewed release.** Run Step 5 for the exact reviewed candidate. Approval creates the controlled public-ready payload; it does not publish. [Technical detail](../../technical/workflows/mortality/approve.qmd)
6. **Publish approved outputs.** Run Step 6 and verify the authoritative public package, release ZIP, catalogue record and website mirror. [Technical detail](../../technical/workflows/mortality/publish.qmd)

After Step 6, inspect the mortality dashboard, tables, methods links and
downloads presentation. A routine data release normally updates the website
from approved public data without changing the page's analysis.

## Stop points and evidence

Stop on a failed check, changed release identity, missing input, implausible
classification or burden results, incomplete disclosure review, approval
mismatch or private content in Git status. Never edit generated mortality
outputs by hand; correct the source or code and rerun.

Retain private source and classification outputs, staging and review material,
approval controls, the publication log and the authoritative public release in
their controlled locations.
